metadata.title: Scoped, Then Rebuilt.
metadata.note: Month three (July 2026, Weeks 10-12, Jul 3-23). Month-as-a-whole structure. Nothing after Jul 23 is referenced anywhere. Third-person, Varun named; no other non-professor names.

beats.narration_text: Month three was defined by judgement rather than volume. A dependency outside Varun's control stayed unresolved, so effort moved to what was controllable: throughput, scope, and then a full change of visual direction — delivered as samples for review.

show.event: Claude composer on cream; greeting 'Hola, HAI' in serif
the ask types itself into the composer
send arms terracotta; running indicator reads 'compiling month three…'
three result lines land

props.command: Show me what Varun built on Medhavy in month three — throughput, scope, and the new direction.
output: twelve planned topics pruned to four

beats.narration_text: The narration dependency was still unresolved and still outside his control. Rather than stall on it or burn hours attempting a workaround, Varun redirected effort to production throughput — building the first four chapters in batch and chaining the render commands so a full set could be produced in one pass.

show.event: eyebrow sets: ADAPTING — PRODUCTION THROUGHPUT
title sets in the serif beneath the terracotta rule
thesis wipes in
three bullets land as named

props.label: ADAPTING — PRODUCTION THROUGHPUT
bullets: First four chapters built in batch.
Render commands chained into a single pass.

beats.narration_text: Chaining the renders is a small change with a real effect. Instead of supervising each build and starting the next by hand, one command produces the set. When a style change arrives later and everything has to be rebuilt, that difference is what makes rebuilding cheap enough to actually do.

show.event: the per-scene invocation sits at the top of the card
the chained form types in beneath it
spark line lands: 'One pass, four chapters.'

props.title: batch production
props.code:
# before — one scene at a time, supervised
render ch01 ; wait ; render ch02 ; wait ...

# after — chained, single pass
render ch01 && render ch02 && render ch03 && render ch04

# rebuild cost drops → a style pivot stays affordable

beats.narration_text: The second decision was subtractive. The original plan covered twelve topics. Varun pruned it to four — the ones that genuinely benefit from animation. That follows the professor's explicit instruction to visualise only what warrants it, and it is the harder call, because cutting eight planned deliverables looks like less work while being the correct one.

show.event: eyebrow sets: EDITORIAL JUDGEMENT
'Twelve topics' sets large in the serif
eight strike through as the pruning is named; four remain in terracotta
thesis and bullets land

props.label: EDITORIAL JUDGEMENT
bullets: Scripts reviewed against the professor's scoping instruction.
Eight topics cut; four retained for production.

beats.narration_text: The narration credential is worth restating plainly, because it spans two months. It was diagnosed as an inactive key, reported to the people who administer the account, and never silently absorbed into the schedule. Work continued around it; the dependency itself simply was not Varun's to close.

show.event: heavy ink rule draws; ground shifts to the dependency register
label sets: 'Narration credential'
span bar fills terracotta across the two-month span
'Ball in: account administrator' sets beneath
resolution line wipes in — reported, not absorbed

props.label: Narration credential
props.resolution: Diagnosed, reported, and worked around — never silently absorbed.

beats.narration_text: Then the direction changed again. Prof. Nik introduced a new production tool and a distinct visual style — a creative call, not a correction. Varun onboarded onto the tool, scoped what the style shift meant technically, and delivered three sample videos in the new style to Prof. Sridhar for review.

show.event: eyebrow sets: NEW DIRECTION — JULY
title sets in the serif
thesis wipes in — a creative call, not a correction
three bullets land, ending on the three samples submitted

props.label: NEW DIRECTION — JULY
props.thesis: A creative-direction change, absorbed and delivered.
bullets: Prof. Nik introduced a new production tool and visual direction.
Style shift scoped technically before rebuilding.
Three sample videos delivered to Prof. Sridhar for review.

beats.narration_text: Three weeks, twenty hours documented in each. Sixty hours for the month. Status: in compliance.

show.event: heading sets: DOCUMENTED HOURS — MONTH THREE
each week's row rules in and its numeral counts to 20
the terracotta total counts up to 60
the compliance status lands with its terracotta dot

beats.narration_text: Month three, then. An upstream dependency handled without stalling. Production batched and chained so rebuilds stay cheap. Twelve planned topics cut to the four that warrant animation. A new tool and a new visual language absorbed inside a fortnight. And three samples delivered for review.
